sources: Ball-by-ball: Cricbuzz full-commentary capture of the 5th ODI (match 161282), parsed into one row per delivery (data/series/nz_ind_2026); innings totals and individual figures checked against Wikipedia's match box ('Indian cricket team in New Zealand in 2026-27', citing Cricinfo) and Cricbuzz's own pace/spin summary line.

Win probability, swings, 'win probability added' and the hidden winner: our own model, fitted on 1,719 men's 50-over ODIs in the Cricsheet archive (2009 onwards, no rain method), validated on held-out matches (accuracy 83%); an indication, not a fact. Drops: the runs a batter scored after a dropped chance (descriptive, not a counterfactual).
4th ODI comparison: Cricbuzz capture of the 4th ODI, with an independent Cricinfo capture agreeing over by over. Figures: analysis/nz_ind_*.py, make_replay_5odi.py.

long.vo: India made two hundred and nine. Our model gave them twenty-two per cent to defend it. They won by twenty-two runs. Here is how it happened, from our own ball-by-ball data.

scene.kicker: INDIA V NEW ZEALAND · 5TH ODI · BAY OVAL
scene.title: India's chance of defending 209.
scene.label: our model, before the chase began · India won by 22 runs

long.vo: This is The Replay Room. The fifth and final one-day international of the series, at Bay Oval, ball by ball.

scene.teaser: India v New Zealand · 5th ODI · 15 November 2026

long.vo: First, India's innings. All out for two hundred and nine in forty-two overs. रोहित शर्मा, विराट कोहली and ऋतुराज गायकवाड़ were gone with thirty-four on the board. Two forty-sixes, from अक्षर पटेल and इशान किशन, kept them alive.
The powerplay was the problem. Thirty-seven for three off the first sixty balls. Seven balls in every ten were dots.

scene.title: Three down, almost nothing scored.
scene.label: off 60 balls · 70% dot balls · 5% boundary balls

long.vo: A last-wicket flurry added twenty-six runs off the final ten balls, with two sixes from अर्शदीप सिंह. It lifted the total. But it moved India's chances by only seven points. They were still the underdogs.

scene.title: Twenty-six off ten balls.
scene.label: 183/9 to 209/10 · India's win probability +7 points (our model)

long.vo: New Zealand needed four point two runs an over, and they never got ahead of it. Four point one in the powerplay, three point eight through the middle overs. By the fortieth over, they were scoring three point nine and needed five and a half.

scene.kicker: NEW ZEALAND'S CHASE · SCORING v REQUIRED
scene.title: Never ahead of the rate.

long.vo: Here is India's chance of winning, over by over. Never above twenty-five per cent in the first twenty overs. Then the wickets: it climbs, falls back, and finally crosses fifty per cent for good at one fifty-eight for seven.

scene.kicker: INDIA'S WIN PROBABILITY DURING NZ'S CHASE · OUR MODEL
scene.title: From 13% to 98%.

long.vo: The biggest swing: over forty point four. नमन धीर, in his second over, gets Mitchell Santner to hole out to अर्शदीप सिंह. Twenty-seven points, in one ball. Just over nine overs earlier, a double: आक़िब नबी gets Bracewell, and the debutant यश ठाकुर bowls Foxcroft next ball. Together, thirty-nine points.

scene.kicker: BIGGEST SWINGS · POINTS OF WIN PROBABILITY · OUR MODEL
scene.title: Three wickets turned it.

long.vo: Then the let-offs. New Zealand dropped अक्षर पटेल on two, and श्रेयस अय्यर on five. Those two batters scored sixty-one more runs. India dropped Foxcroft on five, and Bracewell on eight. They scored thirty-seven. A net twenty-four runs: more than the margin of twenty-two.

scene.kicker: DROPPED CATCHES · RUNS SCORED AFTER THE LET-OFF
scene.title: The drops were worth the match.

long.vo: The hidden winner: नमन धीर. Two overs, four runs, one wicket. By our measure, he was the second most valuable player of the match, behind अर्शदीप सिंह, the Player of the Match, who took three for thirty. And the hidden loser: Jacob Duffy, three wickets, but sixty runs in eight overs.

scene.kicker: HIDDEN WINNER · WIN PROBABILITY ADDED · OUR MODEL
scene.title: Naman Dhir's two overs.
scene.label: 2-0-4-1 · the Santner wicket · second to Arshdeep Singh (+37) · hidden loser: Duffy 3/60 (-20)

long.vo: India leaned on pace: forty overs, at three point eight eight an over. New Zealand's seamers went at five point six four, but their two spinners, Santner and Bracewell, at four point one.

Two days earlier, on the same ground, New Zealand had scored three thirty-three, at six point six six an over. In the fifth, three point eight eight. Their powerplay: seven point two, then four point one. अर्शदीप सिंह's ten overs cost fifty-five runs in the fourth, and thirty in the fifth.

scene.kicker: SAME GROUND, TWO DAYS APART · NZ BATTING
scene.title: What changed at Bay Oval.

long.vo: So how does a twenty-two per cent chance win? A collapse in the middle overs, two let-offs worth more than the margin, and an attack that never let New Zealand get going. Our model says that match goes the other way four times in five.
Which moment turned it for you? Tell us in the comments, and follow for more from The Replay Room.

India vs New Zealand, 5th ODI analysis: how India won at 22%. India made 209; our model gave New Zealand a 78% chance to chase it, and India won by 22 runs. The powerplay collapse, the 27-point turning point at 158/7, the drops worth more than the margin, the hidden winner (Naman Dhir) and what changed at Bay Oval in two days.
